This receiver connects to a [Playwright browser server](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-launch-server) over its WebSocket endpoint and collects browser performance metrics via the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). It only works with Chromium-based browsers managed by Playwright.

## Prerequisites

The receiver speaks the **Playwright protocol** (not raw CDP). You must run a Playwright browser server that exposes a WebSocket endpoint.

### Running a Playwright browser server

Install the `playwright` npm package and its Chromium browser:

```bash
npm install playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Then start a server. The minimal script is:

```javascript
const { chromium } = require("playwright");

(async () => {
  const server = await chromium.launchServer({
    headless: true,
    port: 9222,
    wsPath: "/ws",
  });
  console.log(`WebSocket endpoint: ${server.wsEndpoint()}`);
})();
```

Save this as `server.js` and run it:

```bash
node server.js
# WebSocket endpoint: ws://0.0.0.0:9222/ws
```

The receiver connects to the printed WebSocket endpoint.

> **Note:** The raw Chrome `--remote-debugging-port` endpoint will **not** work. The receiver requires the Playwright protocol layer provided by `chromium.launchServer()`.

### Kubernetes / container deployments

In containerized environments, run the Playwright server as a sidecar or standalone deployment. See [`server.js`](https://github.com/nicholasgasior/playwright-docker/blob/main/server.js) for a production-ready example that includes a health-check HTTP endpoint.

## Configuration

| Parameter | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `endpoint` | yes | — | Playwright WebSocket endpoint URL (e.g. `ws://localhost:9222/ws`) |
| `collection_interval` | no | `30s` | How often to scrape metrics |

### Example

```yaml
receivers:
  playwright:
    endpoint: ws://playwright-server:9222/ws
    collection_interval: 30s
```

## Metrics

### Target counts

| Metric | Description | Unit | Type |
|--------|-------------|------|------|
| `playwright.targets.count` | Active browser targets by type | `{target}` | Gauge |

### Per-page performance metrics

These metrics are collected via the CDP `Performance.getMetrics` command on each page managed by the receiver. Each data point carries `target.url` identifying the page.

| Metric | Description | Unit | Type |
|--------|-------------|------|------|
| `playwright.page.document.count` | Number of documents in the page | `{document}` | Gauge |
| `playwright.page.frame.count` | Number of frames in the page | `{frame}` | Gauge |
| `playwright.page.js_event_listener.count` | Number of JS event listeners | `{listener}` | Gauge |
| `playwright.page.dom_node.count` | Number of DOM nodes | `{node}` | Gauge |
| `playwright.page.js_heap.used_size` | Used JavaScript heap size | `By` | Gauge |
| `playwright.page.js_heap.total_size` | Total JavaScript heap size | `By` | Gauge |
| `playwright.page.layout.count` | Cumulative count of page layouts | `{layout}` | Sum (monotonic) |
| `playwright.page.layout.duration` | Cumulative duration of page layouts | `s` | Sum (monotonic) |
| `playwright.page.recalc_style.count` | Cumulative count of CSS recalculations | `{recalculation}` | Sum (monotonic) |
| `playwright.page.recalc_style.duration` | Cumulative duration of CSS recalculations | `s` | Sum (monotonic) |
| `playwright.page.script.duration` | Cumulative duration of JavaScript execution | `s` | Sum (monotonic) |
| `playwright.page.task.duration` | Cumulative duration of all browser tasks | `s` | Sum (monotonic) |

### Attributes

| Attribute | Description | Present on |
|-----------|-------------|------------|
| `playwright.endpoint` | WebSocket endpoint URL | All metrics |
| `target.type` | Target type (`page`, `service_worker`, `browser`, etc.) | `playwright.targets.count` |
| `target.url` | URL of the page | Per-page metrics |

## How it works

1. The receiver connects to the Playwright server's WebSocket endpoint and initializes a session using the Playwright protocol.
2. It creates a browser-level CDP session to enumerate targets via `Target.getTargets`.
3. It creates its own `BrowserContext` and `Page` to obtain a page-level CDP session. The CDP `Performance` domain is enabled on each page, and `Performance.getMetrics` is called every scrape interval.
4. Pages created through the receiver are tracked via Playwright `__create__` / `__dispose__` events, so metrics are emitted per page with the correct `target.url`.

## Example output

```

playwright.targets.count{playwright.endpoint="ws://localhost:9222/ws", target.type="tab"} 2

playwright.page.dom_node.count{playwright.endpoint="ws://localhost:9222/ws", target.type="page", target.url="https://example.com"} 26
playwright.page.layout.duration{playwright.endpoint="ws://localhost:9222/ws", target.type="page", target.url="https://example.com"} 0.003
```

## Development

### Running integration tests

The integration tests run against a real Chromium instance via a Playwright browser server.

**Setup** (one-time):

```bash
cd receiver/playwrightreceiver
npm install playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

**Run tests:**

```bash
go test -tags=integration -v -timeout 120s ./receiver/playwrightreceiver/...
```

Or point at an already-running Playwright server:

```bash
PLAYWRIGHT_ENDPOINT=ws://localhost:9222/ws go test -tags=integration -v -timeout 120s ./receiver/playwrightreceiver/...
```
